ideas.title: Extract reusable PlatformStudio component to eliminate 6 duplicate studio files
ideas.description: The 6 platform studio files (LinkedInStudio.tsx, YouTubeStudio.tsx, InstagramStudio.tsx, FacebookStudio.tsx, TikTokStudio.tsx, XStudio.tsx) are nearly identical. Each file is ~86 lines with the only difference being the platform config key. This is textbook code duplication that violates DRY principles and makes maintenance difficult - any change must be applied 6 times.
ideas.rationale: Code duplication is one of the highest-impact code smells. These 516 lines (6 × 86) can be reduced to ~100 lines with a single generic PlatformStudio component. This eliminates the risk of inconsistency, reduces merge conflicts, and simplifies testing since only one component needs coverage.
ideas.currentState: 6 nearly identical files, each defining the same interface (StudioProps), same component structure, same hooks usage, differing only in PLATFORM_CONFIGS key
ideas.proposedChange: Create a single generic PlatformStudio component that accepts platform as a prop. Replace all 6 files with a simple re-export pattern or inline usage: <PlatformStudio platform='linkedin' {...props} />
ideas.bestPractice: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) - When multiple pieces of code do the same thing, extract to a single source of truth

ideas.title: Split App.tsx (935 lines) into focused modules using feature-based organization
ideas.description: App.tsx has grown to 935 lines and handles too many concerns: routing (AdminRouter), voice agent wrapper, keyboard shortcuts configuration, navigation state, generation state, refresh logic, onboarding, and modal management. This 'God component' pattern makes the file difficult to understand, test, and maintain.
ideas.rationale: Large root components are a major source of bugs and developer frustration. They create high cognitive load during code reviews, make it difficult to isolate test scenarios, and increase the blast radius of changes. Breaking this into focused modules improves separation of concerns and enables parallel development.
ideas.currentState: Single 935-line file with AppContent (700+ lines), AdminRouter (70 lines), AdminLoadingFallback, VoiceAgentWrapper, and App function all in one file
ideas.proposedChange: Split into: (1) src/routes/AdminRouter.tsx - admin routing logic, (2) src/routes/AppRouter.tsx - main app routing, (3) src/providers/VoiceAgentWrapper.tsx - voice context bridge, (4) src/hooks/useStudioState.ts - studio state management, (5) src/hooks/useAppShortcuts.ts - keyboard shortcuts configuration. App.tsx becomes ~100 lines of composition.
ideas.bestPractice: Single Responsibility Principle - each module should have one reason to change
prerequisites: Ensure test coverage for keyboard shortcuts and voice integration before refactoring

ideas.title: Split database schema.ts (578 lines) into domain-based modules
ideas.description: The server's schema.ts file contains 36 database tables (578 lines) in a single file spanning multiple domains: authentication, profiles, teams, chat, images, admin, agents, billing, and observability. This makes it difficult to navigate, understand relationships, and maintain domain boundaries.
ideas.rationale: Monolithic schema files violate separation of concerns and make it harder to reason about data models. Splitting by domain enables better encapsulation, clearer ownership, easier code review, and aligns with the planned feature co-location strategy mentioned in CLAUDE.md.
ideas.currentState: Single 578-line file with 36 tables covering 9+ domains with inline section comments as the only organization
ideas.proposedChange: Split into domain modules: server/src/db/schema/auth.ts (users, sessions, tokens), server/src/db/schema/profiles.ts (profiles, preferences, apiKeys), server/src/db/schema/teams.ts (teams, members, brands), server/src/db/schema/chat.ts (conversations, messages, transcripts), server/src/db/schema/gallery.ts (images, designs), server/src/db/schema/admin.ts (adminUsers, audit, rateLimit), server/src/db/schema/agents.ts (configs, skills, mcp), server/src/db/schema/billing.ts (tiers, credits, transactions), server/src/db/schema/observability.ts (traces, metrics, logs). Create server/src/db/schema/index.ts barrel export.
ideas.bestPractice: Domain-Driven Design - organize code around business domains, not technical layers
prerequisites: Ensure all Drizzle queries use explicit imports to avoid circular dependencies

ideas.title: Reduce eslint-disable directives (40 occurrences) through proper typing and refactoring
ideas.description: There are 40 eslint-disable comments across 28 files, indicating systematic bypassing of linting rules. The most common disables are for @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any and unused variables. This technical debt accumulates silently and undermines the value of having strict TypeScript configuration.
ideas.rationale: ESLint rules exist to prevent bugs and maintain code quality. Disabling them should be exceptional, not routine. High eslint-disable counts indicate either: (1) rules that don't fit the project (should be adjusted in config), or (2) code that needs refactoring to meet standards. Addressing this reduces runtime errors and improves IDE support.
ideas.currentState: 40 eslint-disable comments across 28 files, with AIContext.tsx having 3, ImageGallery.tsx having 4, and ExportPanel.tsx having 4. Many are disabling 'no-explicit-any' and 'no-unused-vars'.
ideas.proposedChange: Audit each eslint-disable: (1) For 'no-explicit-any' - add proper TypeScript generics or interface definitions, (2) For 'no-unused-vars' - remove unused code or use underscore prefix convention, (3) For legitimate exceptions - add inline explanation comment. Target: reduce from 40 to <10 necessary exceptions.
ideas.bestPractice: TypeScript strictness - leverage the type system for safety; eslint-disable should be rare and documented

ideas.title: Extract SettingsModal sections (631 lines) into focused sub-components
ideas.description: SettingsModal.tsx has grown to 631 lines handling multiple concerns: API key management for 3 providers (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Replicate), model selection dropdowns for 4 model types, connection testing UI, session timeout configuration, and save/validation logic. The component is difficult to test in isolation and changes to one section risk affecting others.
ideas.rationale: Large modal components are particularly problematic because they often contain complex state management and validation logic that becomes intertwined. Breaking this into sub-components enables focused unit tests, reduces cognitive load, and enables reuse (e.g., APIKeyInput could be used in onboarding).
ideas.currentState: Single 631-line component with inline ConnectionStatus component, 3 API key sections with similar structure, 4 model dropdown sections with similar structure, and mixed concerns
ideas.proposedChange: Extract into focused components: (1) src/components/features/settings/APIKeySection.tsx - reusable API key input with test button and status, (2) src/components/features/settings/ModelSelector.tsx - dropdown with model list and description, (3) src/components/features/settings/ConnectionStatus.tsx - extracted and properly typed, (4) src/components/features/settings/useSettingsForm.ts - custom hook for form state and validation. SettingsModal becomes ~150 lines of composition.
ideas.bestPractice: Component composition - build complex UIs from simple, focused, reusable components

ideas.title: Add database indexes for frequently queried columns
ideas.description: The database schema lacks indexes on columns that are heavily queried with filters and ordering. The images, chatMessages, designs, and chatConversations tables are queried with WHERE clauses on userId, generationType, isFavorite, and LIKE search on prompt, with ORDER BY on createdAt/lastMessageAt/updatedAt. Without indexes, these queries perform full table scans.
ideas.rationale: Every image gallery load, chat history fetch, designs list, and conversation retrieval currently scans the entire table. With 10,000+ rows per table, queries can take 100-500ms. Adding composite indexes would reduce this to <10ms. This is the highest-impact database optimization available.
ideas.currentMetric: Full table scan on every query (O(n) for n rows)
ideas.expectedImprovement: 10-50x faster queries with index lookups (O(log n))
ideas.implementation:
1. Add composite index on images(userId, createdAt DESC) for gallery listing
2. Add index on images(userId, isFavorite) for favorites filter
3. Add index on images(userId, generationType) for type filter
4. Add GIN index on designs(tags) for array containment queries
5. Add index on chatConversations(userId, lastMessageAt DESC) for conversation list
6. Add index on chatMessages(conversationId, createdAt) for message retrieval
7. Generate and run migration with Drizzle Kit
ideas.tradeoffs: Slight increase in write latency (~1-2ms per INSERT) and storage overhead. Worth it for read-heavy workload pattern.

ideas.title: Memoize useCanvas() combined hook to prevent cascade re-renders
ideas.description: The useCanvas() combined hook in src/context/canvas/index.ts creates a new object literal on every call (lines 138-200), aggregating 5 sub-contexts without memoization. This defeats the purpose of the context split architecture and causes all consumers to re-render whenever ANY sub-context changes.
ideas.rationale: The application correctly split CanvasContext into 5 focused contexts (CanvasStateContext, ElementsContext, LayerContext, HistoryContext, ImageContext). However, the combined useCanvas() hook returns a new object on every render, negating the optimization. Components using useCanvas() will re-render when elements change, even if they only need canvas state. This is visible in App.tsx where useCanvas() is called in VoiceAgentWrapper.
ideas.currentMetric: New object created on every useCanvas() call, cascading re-renders through context tree
ideas.expectedImprovement: ~40-60% reduction in re-renders for canvas-dependent components, smoother canvas interactions
ideas.tradeoffs: Complex dependency array for useMemo; migration to specific hooks is cleaner but more invasive

ideas.title: Implement parallel AI provider fallback with smart timeouts
ideas.description: The generateImage function in src/services/imageGenerationService.ts uses sequential try/catch fallbacks (Nano Banana Pro -> Flux Schnell -> Flux Dev). Each provider attempt must complete or timeout before the next begins, creating worst-case latencies of 15-30+ seconds when providers are slow or unavailable.
ideas.rationale: Current sequential approach: if primary times out in 10s, fallback 1 times out in 10s, users wait 20s before fallback 2 even starts. Image generation is the core user flow, and these delays feel broken. Using Promise.any() with staggered starts could resolve with first success while maintaining cost control.
ideas.currentMetric: Sequential fallback: 15-30s worst-case generation time during provider issues
ideas.expectedImprovement: ~60-70% reduction in worst-case generation time; <10s even during partial outages
ideas.implementation:
1. Implement tiered parallel strategy with AbortController:
   ```typescript
   const controller = new AbortController();
   const tier1 = tryProvider('nano-banana-pro', controller.signal);
   
   const result = await Promise.any([
     tier1,
     tier1.catch(() => sleep(3000)).then(() => tryProvider('flux-schnell', controller.signal)),
     tier1.catch(() => sleep(6000)).then(() => tryProvider('flux-dev', controller.signal))
   ]);
   
   controller.abort(); // Cancel remaining requests
   ```
2. Track provider health metrics to dynamically adjust tier delays
3. Consider cost implications (parallel requests may increase API spend)
4. Add circuit breaker pattern for repeatedly failing providers
ideas.tradeoffs: May increase API costs if multiple providers are called simultaneously; requires AbortController support in API client

ideas.title: Move tag filtering from JavaScript to PostgreSQL with GIN index
ideas.description: The GET /designs endpoint in server/src/routes/designs.ts (lines 37-44) fetches ALL user designs then filters by tags in JavaScript. This wastes database bandwidth and memory, especially as users accumulate designs.
ideas.rationale: Post-query filtering loads unnecessary data from the database. The code fetches up to 50 designs, then filters in JS: `filteredDesigns = userDesigns.filter(d => d.tags?.some(...))`. PostgreSQL's array operations with GIN indexes are optimized for exactly this use case. Moving filter to SQL leverages query planning and reduces data transfer.
ideas.currentMetric: All designs fetched to memory, then filtered; O(n*m) JS filtering
ideas.expectedImprovement: ~50-80% reduction in data transfer; database handles filtering with O(log n) index lookups
ideas.tradeoffs: PostgreSQL-specific syntax; requires migration deployment; need to ensure tag normalization (lowercase) at write time

ideas.title: Implement localStorage cleanup and batching for performance metrics
ideas.description: The trackModelPerformance function in src/services/modelRouter.ts stores up to 1000 metric entries in localStorage (line 23). Each tracked metric triggers a full read-parse-push-write cycle. With heavy usage, this array can reach 200-400KB, causing synchronous localStorage operations to block the main thread.
ideas.rationale: localStorage is synchronous and blocks the main thread. The performance_log array is read and rewritten on every AI operation. With objects containing timestamps, model IDs, latency, and success rates, 1000 entries creates significant payload. This creates UI jank during the exact moments users are waiting for AI results.
ideas.currentMetric: Synchronous localStorage read/write (200-400KB) on every metric tracked
ideas.expectedImprovement: ~70% reduction in localStorage payload; eliminate storage-related UI jank
ideas.tradeoffs: Metrics may be lost on hard close before flush; requires migration strategy for existing users

ideas.title: Encrypt API keys at rest in database
ideas.description: User API keys (Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Replicate) are stored as plain text in the `user_api_keys` table in `server/src/db/schema.ts`. If the database is compromised, all user API keys are immediately exposed. API keys are high-value secrets that grant access to paid services and could result in significant financial damage if leaked.
ideas.rationale: API keys are equivalent to credentials and should be encrypted at rest. A database breach, SQL injection, or insider threat would expose all stored API keys without encryption. Users trust the platform with their sensitive credentials, and plain text storage violates security best practices and compliance requirements.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
ideas.currentRisk: Database compromise exposes all user API keys in plain text, enabling attackers to abuse users' paid AI service accounts
ideas.remediation: Implement application-level encryption for API keys before storing in the database. Use AES-256-GCM with a key derived from a secret stored in environment variables or a key management service (GCP Secret Manager). Create encrypt/decrypt utility functions in a new `server/src/lib/crypto.ts` file. Decrypt only when making API calls server-side. Never return decrypted keys to the client.

ideas.title: Add explicit HttpOnly and SameSite attributes to session cookies
ideas.description: The Lucia session cookie configuration in `server/src/lib/auth.ts` only sets the `secure` attribute for production. The `httpOnly` and `sameSite` attributes are not explicitly configured, relying on Lucia defaults that may vary. Explicit configuration ensures consistent session security across all environments.
ideas.rationale: HttpOnly prevents JavaScript access to cookies, mitigating XSS-based session theft. SameSite=Lax or Strict prevents CSRF attacks by ensuring cookies are not sent in cross-origin requests. While Lucia likely sets reasonable defaults, explicit configuration ensures predictable security behavior and makes security audits clearer.
ideas.currentRisk: XSS vulnerabilities could lead to session hijacking if cookies are accessible to JavaScript. Cross-site request forgery may be possible without explicit SameSite restriction.
ideas.remediation: Update Lucia configuration to explicitly set: `sessionCookie: { attributes: { secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production', httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax' } }`. Consider 'strict' for sameSite if cross-site navigation with auth isn't required.

ideas.title: Add rate limiting to public sharing endpoints
ideas.description: The public sharing routes (`/api/sharing/public/*`) in `server/src/routes/sharing.ts` lack rate limiting, making them vulnerable to brute force attacks on share tokens, comment spam on shared designs, and enumeration attacks. Unlike auth and AI endpoints which have rate limiting, these public routes have no protection.
ideas.rationale: Share tokens (UUIDs) are the only authorization mechanism for accessing shared content. While UUIDs are hard to guess, systematic requests can enumerate valid tokens over time. Comment endpoints without rate limits enable spam flooding that degrades user experience.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
ideas.currentRisk: Unlimited requests to public sharing endpoints allow brute force attacks on share tokens, comment spam flooding, and resource exhaustion. No monitoring of suspicious access patterns.
ideas.remediation: 1. Apply rate limiting middleware to all `/api/sharing/public/*` routes. 2. Suggested limits: 30 requests/minute for design access (GET), 10 comments/minute per IP (POST). 3. Add `publicRateLimit` and `commentRateLimit` to rateLimit.ts. 4. Consider CAPTCHA for comment submission. 5. Log rate limit violations to detect attacks.

ideas.title: Implement input sanitization for comment content
ideas.description: The comment creation endpoint in `server/src/routes/sharing.ts` (lines 79-115) accepts `content` and `author_name` directly from user input without sanitization or validation. While React escapes output by default, stored XSS could occur if this data is rendered in non-React contexts (emails, PDF exports, admin panels, future integrations).
ideas.rationale: Defense in depth requires sanitizing user input at the storage layer, not just relying on output encoding. Malicious payloads stored in the database persist and affect all viewers. Content could be rendered in multiple contexts where XSS protection varies.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Stored XSS)
ideas.currentRisk: Malicious JavaScript in comments could execute in admin dashboards, email notifications, or future integrations that don't properly escape output. No content length limits enable DoS via oversized comments.
ideas.remediation: 1. Add server-side sanitization using a library like `sanitize-html` or `xss`. 2. Strip HTML tags from comment content. 3. Limit content length (e.g., max 2000 characters). 4. Validate author_name against an allowlist of characters (alphanumeric + spaces). 5. Add validation helper: `const sanitizeComment = (content: string) => content.slice(0, 2000).replace(/<[^>]*>/g, '');`

ideas.title: Implement email verification status tracking and enforcement
ideas.description: The authentication system generates and sends email verification tokens but never actually marks users as verified. The `users` table in `server/src/db/schema.ts` lacks an `email_verified` column, and the verify-email endpoint in `server/src/routes/auth.ts` only deletes the token without updating user status. No routes enforce verification before allowing access to sensitive features.
ideas.rationale: Email verification ensures users control the email address they register with, preventing account squatting and enabling secure password recovery. Without tracking verification status, malicious users could register with others' email addresses and gain trust. This is explicitly noted as a TODO in the codebase (auth.ts line 239-241).
ideas.currentRisk: Users can operate accounts with unverified email addresses, potentially impersonating others. Password recovery could send reset links to attacker-controlled addresses if email ownership isn't verified. No audit trail of verified vs unverified users.
ideas.remediation: 1) Add `emailVerified: boolean('email_verified').default(false)` to the users schema. 2) Update the verify-email endpoint to: `await db.update(users).set({ emailVerified: true }).where(eq(users.id, token.userId));` 3) Add middleware to restrict certain actions (API key management, sharing, team invites) to verified users only. 4) Consider sending re-verification emails when email is changed.

ideas.title: Add Teams CRUD Router
ideas.description: Create a full CRUD API router for the teams and teamMembers tables. The database schema already defines teams and teamMembers tables with proper relationships, but no API routes exist. This would enable team creation, member management, and role assignment.
ideas.rationale: The teams and teamMembers tables exist in server/src/db/schema.ts with full schema definitions (team name, owner, members with roles). The CRUD router pattern is well-established in brands.ts, designs.ts, and images.ts - this is a direct copy with table name changes. Teams are referenced by brandProfiles (team_id FK exists), showing the data model is ready.
existing_patterns: server/src/routes/brands.ts - Full CRUD with ownership verification
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Create server/src/routes/teams.ts following brands.ts structure exactly. 2. Import teams and teamMembers from schema. 3. Add routes: GET / (list user's teams), POST / (create team), GET /:id (get team with members), PATCH /:id (update team), DELETE /:id (delete team), POST /:id/members (add member), DELETE /:id/members/:userId (remove member), PATCH /:id/members/:userId (change role). 4. Register in index.ts with app.route('/api/teams', teamRouter).

ideas.title: Add Voice Transcripts API Route
ideas.description: Create an API route to list, search, and export voice transcripts. The voiceTranscripts table stores all voice interactions but users have no way to review, search, or export their voice history.
ideas.rationale: The voiceTranscripts table exists with fields for userId, conversationId, role, content, audioDurationMs, toolCalls, and provider. The chatMessages route (server/src/routes/chat.ts) already provides identical functionality for chat messages. This is a small extension applying the same pattern to voice data.
existing_patterns: server/src/routes/chat.ts - Messages list with conversation scoping
server/src/routes/prompts.ts - List with search and category filters
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Create server/src/routes/voice.ts with Hono router. 2. Add GET /transcripts endpoint with filters: date range, provider (gemini/openai), search in content. 3. Add GET /transcripts/export for JSON/CSV export of transcript history. 4. Follow prompts.ts for search/filter query param patterns. 5. Include pagination with limit/offset. 6. Register in index.ts.

ideas.title: Add Design Owner Comments Management
ideas.description: Enable design owners to view, resolve, and delete comments on their designs. Currently comments are only accessible via shared links - owners cannot manage feedback on their own designs.
ideas.rationale: The comments table exists and is used via sharing.ts public routes. The isResolved field exists but has no toggle route. Design owners should be able to: list all comments on their designs, mark comments as resolved, delete inappropriate comments. The toggle pattern exists in prompts.ts (toggle-favorite) and designs.ts (toggle-public).
existing_patterns: server/src/routes/sharing.ts - Comment creation on shared designs
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add authenticated routes to sharing.ts: GET /designs/:designId/comments (list comments for owned design), POST /comments/:id/resolve (toggle isResolved), DELETE /comments/:id (delete comment). 2. Each route verifies design ownership via designs table userId check. 3. Follow the existing toggle-favorite pattern from prompts.ts for the resolve toggle. 4. Add filters for resolved/unresolved in list endpoint.

ideas.title: Add Batch Delete Designs Command
ideas.description: Add a voice/AI command for batch deleting multiple designs from the gallery. The pattern exists for batch operations on canvas elements but not for gallery cleanup.
ideas.rationale: BatchDeleteElementsCommand, BatchUpscaleCommand, and BatchRemoveBackgroundCommand already exist in the command system demonstrating the batch pattern. Users may want to clean up multiple old designs at once. The Command interface and ActionExecutor registration pattern are well established.
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. In galleryCommands.ts, add BatchDeleteDesignsCommand class implementing Command. 2. Accept args: { design_ids: string[] }. 3. Loop through IDs calling deleteDesignFromDb for each, collecting results/errors like BatchUpscaleCommand does. 4. Return aggregated result: { success: X, errors: Y }. 5. Register in actionExecutor.ts with this.registerCommand(new BatchDeleteDesignsCommand()). 6. Add to ToolSchemas for validation.

ideas.title: Implement LangfuseService getDailyMetrics
ideas.description: Complete the stubbed getDailyMetrics method in LangfuseService to aggregate and return daily usage statistics from Langfuse traces.
ideas.rationale: LangfuseService.getDailyMetrics() exists but returns empty array with comment 'for now, let's focus on Traces'. The getTraces method shows the working pattern for Langfuse API calls with proper auth headers. The dailyStats table exists in schema for storing aggregated metrics. AdminObservability page likely expects this data.
existing_patterns: server/src/services/langfuse.ts - getTraces method with Langfuse API auth
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. In langfuse.ts getDailyMetrics, follow getTraces pattern for API calls. 2. Fetch traces for date range, aggregate by day: totalRequests, totalTokens, uniqueUsers, errorCount. 3. Option A: Compute from traces API if Langfuse supports date filtering. Option B: Store daily aggregates in dailyStats table via scheduled job and query from DB. 4. Return array of { date, metrics } objects matching dailyStats schema. 5. Add error handling matching getTraces pattern.

ideas.title: Add visible focus indicators for keyboard navigation
ideas.description: Replace focus:outline-none with visible focus rings on interactive elements across the app to improve keyboard accessibility and WCAG compliance.
ideas.rationale: Analysis found 107 instances of 'focus:outline-none' across 55 files, with many buttons and inputs removing focus indicators without providing visible alternatives. This creates accessibility barriers for keyboard users and fails WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 2.4.7 (Focus Visible). The app already has good patterns in some components (PlatformCard.tsx uses focus:ring-2 focus:ring-sky-500/50) but this isn't consistent.
ideas.current_state: ChatInput.tsx (line 93) has 'focus:outline-none focus:border-white/20' which removes the default focus ring with only a subtle border change. GenerativeSidebar.tsx textarea (line 395) has 'focus:border-pink-500 focus:ring-2' which is good. SettingsModal.tsx inputs (9 occurrences) use focus:outline-none. Many buttons across the app use 'focus:outline-none' without replacement focus indicators.
ideas.proposed_change: Create a standardized focus utility class in Tailwind config or styles.ts: 'focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-yellow-400/50 focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-stone-950 focus:outline-none'. Use focus-visible (not focus) to only show for keyboard navigation. Apply to all buttons, inputs, links. Add to PlatformCard pattern as standard. For high-contrast mode, add 'contrast-more:focus-visible:ring-current contrast-more:focus-visible:ring-offset-0' as fallback per Design System Section 3.2.
ideas.user_benefit: Keyboard users can clearly see which element is focused while navigating. Screen reader users get proper focus management. App becomes WCAG 2.1 AA compliant for focus visibility. Power users who prefer keyboard navigation have better experience.

ideas.title: Redesign ErrorBoundary with branded error page
ideas.description: Transform the basic ErrorBoundary fallback UI from stark white/red text to a polished, on-brand error recovery screen with retry options and support links.
ideas.rationale: The current ErrorBoundary.tsx (lines 30-40) renders a jarring white background with red text that breaks the dark theme experience. When errors occur, users see 'Something went wrong' with raw error details - this looks broken and unprofessional. Error states are critical UX moments that can either frustrate users or build trust through graceful handling.
ideas.current_state: ErrorBoundary.tsx line 32 shows: 'p-5 text-red-600 bg-white' with raw error stack traces in a <details> element. This creates visual whiplash from the dark app theme. No recovery actions are offered. Error details are shown raw without explanation. The component lacks role='alert' aria attributes.
ideas.proposed_change: Redesign the fallback UI: (1) Use dark theme colors (bg-stone-950 text-white) matching the app, (2) Add Signal-branded error illustration or icon (existing material-icons: error_outline), (3) Show user-friendly message: 'Something unexpected happened' with 'We've logged this issue and are looking into it', (4) Add 'Try Again' button that calls window.location.reload(), (5) Add 'Go to Dashboard' button, (6) Add 'Report Issue' link to support, (7) Collapse technical details into an expandable section for debugging, (8) Add role='alert' aria-live='assertive' for screen readers. Style buttons with existing BTN_NEU_SOLID patterns.
ideas.user_benefit: Errors feel handled rather than catastrophic. Users have clear recovery paths instead of being stuck. Consistent dark theme maintains immersion. Technical details available for debugging without overwhelming regular users. Professional error handling builds trust in the app.

ideas.title: Add swipe-to-dismiss gesture for mobile GenerativeSidebar bottom sheet
ideas.description: Implement native-feeling swipe-down gesture to dismiss the mobile AI Studio bottom sheet, matching iOS/Android system sheet behaviors.
ideas.rationale: GenerativeSidebar.tsx (lines 587-651) renders as a bottom sheet on mobile with a drag handle indicator (line 593: 'w-10 h-1 bg-zinc-700 rounded-full') but swiping down doesn't dismiss it - users must tap the X button. Mobile users expect bottom sheets to be swipe-dismissible based on iOS/Android system behaviors. The drag handle visual suggests swipe functionality that doesn't exist.
ideas.current_state: Mobile bottom sheet has visual drag handle but no gesture support. Close requires tapping the small X button (line 596-599). The sheet has max-h-[80vh] but no dynamic height based on swipe. The drag handle indicator is decorative only. Touch targets are good (min-w-[40px] min-h-[40px]) but the primary dismissal UX is suboptimal.
ideas.proposed_change: Add swipe-to-dismiss using touch events or a lightweight library: (1) Track touchstart/touchmove/touchend on the header area, (2) If user swipes down > 100px from drag handle, trigger dismiss with spring animation, (3) Add visual feedback during drag (sheet follows finger), (4) Add velocity-based dismiss (fast swipe triggers close), (5) Add partial drag state where sheet snaps back if swipe < threshold, (6) Use will-change: transform for 60fps performance per Design System Section 7.2. Can implement with pure JS or use existing useSpring hook pattern from AppShell.tsx.
ideas.user_benefit: Mobile users can dismiss the sidebar naturally with one-handed swipe gesture. Reduces accidental taps on small close button. Matches user mental model from other apps. Faster workflow on mobile. The drag handle becomes functional, not just decorative.

ideas.title: Add descriptive alt text to PlatformCard images for screen readers
ideas.description: Replace empty alt attributes on platform card images with descriptive text that conveys the platform identity to screen reader users.
ideas.rationale: PlatformCard.tsx line 136 has alt='' on the 3D platform images. While the button has focus styling and the Icon component provides some context, screen reader users navigating the dashboard hear only the button text without understanding the visual representation. WCAG 1.1.1 requires meaningful alt text or proper aria-hidden treatment.
ideas.current_state: PlatformCard.tsx line 136: . The empty alt tells screen readers to ignore the image, but the image is decorative AND informative (it shows the platform logo). The surrounding button only contains Icon + platform name + description. A blind user would understand 'LinkedIn Professional' but miss the visual branding context that sighted users get from the 3D images.
ideas.proposed_change: Update alt text to be descriptive: alt={`${config.name} logo - 3D illustration`}. This provides: (1) Platform identity confirmation, (2) Image type context (3D illustration), (3) Richer browsing experience for screen reader users. Alternatively, use aria-hidden='true' on the image if we consider it purely decorative AND add aria-label to the button: aria-label={`Create content for ${config.name} - ${config.description}`}. Also add role='img' for semantic clarity.
ideas.user_benefit: Screen reader users get complete information about each platform card. Blind users understand the visual design language of the app. WCAG 1.1.1 compliance improves. More inclusive experience for users with visual impairments.

ideas.title: Standardize skeleton loader styles with shimmer animation
ideas.description: Unify all skeleton loading states to use the shimmer variant consistently for a more polished perceived-performance experience.
ideas.rationale: Skeleton.tsx defines both 'rect' (animate-pulse bg-white/5) and 'shimmer' (uses .skeleton CSS class) variants. Analysis shows inconsistent usage: App.tsx line 684 uses <Skeleton height={200}> (defaults to rect), while DashboardPage line 326 also uses non-shimmer. The shimmer effect creates a more premium loading experience that matches the Life OS Design System's luxury aesthetic.
ideas.current_state: Skeleton.tsx (lines 25-27) defaults to 'rect' variant with animate-pulse. The 'shimmer' variant exists but requires explicit variant='shimmer'. Throughout the app, skeleton usages like App.tsx lines 656-665, 673, 683-685 all use default rect variant. The ImageCardSkeleton (Skeleton.tsx lines 49-58) also uses default non-shimmer. This creates inconsistent loading experiences across different views.
ideas.proposed_change: Update Skeleton component: (1) Change default variant from 'rect' to 'shimmer' in Skeleton.tsx line 16, (2) Ensure .skeleton CSS class in index.css has performant shimmer animation (linear gradient moving left-to-right), (3) Add variant='pulse' as explicit option for cases where shimmer isn't wanted, (4) Update ImageCardSkeleton to use shimmer, (5) Verify shimmer respects prefers-reduced-motion via CSS. The shimmer animation should be subtle (10-20% opacity variation) not flashy.
ideas.user_benefit: Consistent, premium-feeling loading states across all views. Shimmer effect provides better perceived performance by suggesting content is 'streaming in'. Cohesive design language reinforces app quality. Reduced cognitive load from consistent patterns.

ideas.title: Add Toast Notification Auto-Dismiss Progress Indicator
ideas.description: Add a visual progress bar at the bottom of toast notifications showing remaining time before auto-dismiss, pausing when user hovers.
ideas.rationale: Toast.tsx implements pause/resume on hover via ToastContext but users have no visual feedback about when notifications will disappear. This creates uncertainty - users can't tell if they have time to read the message. A shrinking progress bar creates predictability and leverages the existing hover-pause functionality.
ideas.current_state: Toast.tsx (lines 143-155) calls pauseToast/resumeToast on hover but this is invisible to users. The toast duration is configurable but not visualized. Users cannot see that hovering pauses the timer. The component uses transform-based animations which is good for performance.
ideas.proposed_change: Add a thin progress bar: (1) Create new div at bottom of toast: className='absolute bottom-0 left-0 h-0.5 origin-left' (2) Add CSS animation: @keyframes toast-progress { from { transform: scaleX(1) } to { transform: scaleX(0) } } (3) Set animation-duration to match toast.duration (4) Pause animation on hover via animation-play-state: paused (5) Use brand colors per toast type (orange for info/success, red for error) (6) Add motion-reduce:hidden for accessibility. Implementation: style={{ animationDuration: `${toast.duration}ms`, animationPlayState: isPaused ? 'paused' : 'running' }}
ideas.user_benefit: Users gain visual certainty about notification timing. The hover-pause feature becomes discoverable. Reduces notification anxiety especially for error messages. Creates a more polished, professional interaction pattern.

ideas.title: Increase MainNav Active State Visual Contrast
ideas.description: Strengthen the visual distinction between active and inactive navigation items by increasing indicator width, background opacity, and adding aria-current attribute.
ideas.rationale: MainNav.tsx uses a 1px-wide yellow bar (line 94-103) and subtle 12% opacity background for active state. This provides insufficient contrast ratio for users with color vision deficiencies (8% of males). The hover arrow starts at opacity: 0 making the affordance invisible. WCAG requires 3:1 contrast for state indicators.
ideas.current_state: MainNav.tsx line 94 sets active indicator height to 24px but width is only w-1 (4px). Line 83-86 shows active background is rgba(250, 204, 21, 0.12) which is barely visible. The ArrowRight indicator (lines 134-142) starts at opacity: 0, wasting the affordance.
ideas.proposed_change: Increase visual weight: (1) Change indicator width from w-1 to w-1.5 (6px) on line 93 (2) Increase active background opacity from 0.12 to 0.20 on line 84 (3) Add fontWeight: 700 for active text (currently 600) on line 127 (4) Set arrow initial opacity to 0.3 instead of 0 on line 137 (5) Add aria-current='page' to active button for screen readers (6) Add optional left-side highlight effect for redundant encoding
ideas.user_benefit: Users immediately identify their current location without relying solely on color. Color blind users can navigate confidently. Screen readers announce current page. The nav becomes usable by a wider range of abilities and preferences.

ideas.title: Add Dashboard Loading Skeleton with Content Structure Preview
ideas.description: Replace the simple spinner fallback in App.tsx with a content-aware skeleton that mirrors the dashboard layout structure during initial load.
ideas.rationale: App.tsx lines 411-420 show a Suspense fallback with just a spinning icon and 'Loading Signal...' text. This provides no spatial preview of upcoming content. Research shows skeleton screens improve perceived performance by 10-20% by showing layout structure immediately.
ideas.current_state: App.tsx DashboardPage fallback (lines 411-420) shows: 'Loading Signal...' with spinning dashboard icon. Meanwhile, the existing Skeleton component with shimmer variant is available but unused here. Users see a minimal loader then sudden content pop-in which feels jarring.
ideas.proposed_change: Create DashboardSkeleton component: (1) New file: src/components/dashboard/DashboardSkeleton.tsx (2) Mirror grid layout: 2x3 grid of PlatformCard skeletons (3) Include header skeleton with user menu placeholder (4) Show recent designs section skeleton (5) Use existing <Skeleton variant='shimmer' /> (6) Match spacing/padding of actual dashboard. Replace App.tsx fallback with <DashboardSkeleton />. Add aria-busy='true' aria-label='Loading dashboard' for accessibility.
ideas.user_benefit: Dashboard appears to load instantly with structure preview. Users understand what's coming before content renders. Perceived performance improves significantly. Creates a premium, polished first impression.

ideas.title: Animate EmptyState Illustration with Brand Colors
ideas.description: Transform the static gray EmptyState icon into an animated, on-brand illustration using the Signal Design System's orange/emerald palette.
ideas.rationale: EmptyState.tsx uses text-zinc-600 for the icon and sky-500/teal-500 for the CTA button - violating the Anti-Slop color guidelines (no teal per index.css line 12-13). Empty states are critical UX moments. The static gray icon feels lifeless and the off-brand button breaks visual consistency.
ideas.current_state: EmptyState.tsx line 15: SVG icon uses text-zinc-600 (gray). Line 32: CTA button uses 'from-sky-500 to-teal-500' which is NOT Anti-Slop compliant. No animation on the illustration. No aria-label for screen reader context.
ideas.proposed_change: Brand-align EmptyState: (1) Change icon color from text-zinc-600 to text-orange-400 on line 15 (2) Add animate-pulse-glow class (exists in index.css) to icon container (3) Change CTA button to 'from-orange-500 to-amber-500' (Anti-Slop compliant) (4) Add aria-label='No items found' to container div (5) Add role='status' for screen reader announcement (6) Consider using Lucide Sparkles icon for more visual interest. The animation should be subtle per prefers-reduced-motion.
ideas.user_benefit: Empty states feel intentional and on-brand rather than like an error. Users have clearer calls-to-action. Consistent color palette builds trust. Screen reader users understand the empty state context.

ideas.title: Add Keyboard Shortcut Hints to Tooltip-Worthy Buttons
ideas.description: Enhance button tooltips to include keyboard shortcut hints where shortcuts exist, improving discoverability of power user features.
ideas.rationale: The app has comprehensive keyboard shortcuts (useKeyboardShortcuts hook, KeyboardShortcutsModal) but they're hidden until users open the modal (?). Header.tsx buttons have title attributes but don't mention shortcuts. Power users discover shortcuts faster when hints are visible during normal use.
ideas.current_state: Header.tsx refresh button (line 82) has title='Refresh' with no shortcut hint. GenerativeSidebar.tsx has various action buttons without shortcut hints. The shortcuts object in App.tsx (lines 301-364) defines many shortcuts but they're not surfaced in UI tooltips. KeyboardShortcutsModal exists but requires explicit opening.
ideas.proposed_change: Add shortcut hints to tooltips: (1) Update Header refresh button: title='Refresh (Ctrl+R)' (2) Add to GenerativeSidebar generate button: title='Generate Background (Ctrl+Enter)' (3) Create helper: formatTooltip(label: string, shortcut?: string) => shortcut ? `${label} (${shortcut})` : label (4) Add data-shortcut attributes for potential future keyboard hint overlay (5) Consider subtle keyboard icon in button for discoverable shortcuts. Platform-aware: show Cmd on Mac, Ctrl on Windows.
ideas.user_benefit: Power users discover shortcuts naturally while using the app. Reduces time to learn advanced features. Users feel more productive as they adopt shortcuts. Creates perception of a thoughtfully designed professional tool.

ideas.title: Modal Close Button Touch Target Size
ideas.description: Add proper 44x44px minimum touch target to close buttons in SettingsModal and similar modals to meet iOS HIG and Android Material Design accessibility guidelines.
ideas.rationale: The close button in SettingsModal currently only displays an icon without a proper touch target wrapper. On mobile devices, small touch targets cause frustration and accessibility issues. The codebase already has touch-target utilities in index.css (line 357-365) and uses them in Toast.tsx close button, but they're not consistently applied to modal close buttons.
ideas.current_state: SettingsModal.tsx close button uses `absolute top-4 right-4 text-zinc-500 hover:text-white transition` with just an icon span, resulting in a touch target of approximately 24x24px (icon size only). Compare to Toast.tsx line 258-267 which properly uses `min-w-[44px] min-h-[44px]` for the close button.
ideas.proposed_change: Update the close button className to: `absolute top-4 right-4 min-w-[44px] min-h-[44px] flex items-center justify-center text-zinc-500 hover:text-white hover:bg-white/10 rounded-full transition focus-ring`. This matches the pattern already established in Toast.tsx and Header.tsx refresh button.
ideas.user_benefit: Easier to tap close button on mobile devices, better accessibility for users with motor impairments, consistent with other buttons in the app like Toast close button.

ideas.title: Custom Select Dropdown Arrow Indicator
ideas.description: Add a visible dropdown arrow indicator to all native select elements that have appearance-none styling, making it clear they are interactive dropdown menus.
ideas.rationale: The SettingsModal uses appearance-none on select elements to reset native styling, but doesn't add a custom dropdown arrow. This makes select fields visually indistinguishable from text inputs, causing confusion about their interactive nature. Users may not realize they can click to see options. The GenerativeSidebar model selector (lines 211-234) shows the correct pattern with an expand_more icon.
ideas.current_state: SettingsModal.tsx select elements (e.g., chat-model-select line 378-388, image-gen-model-select line 410-420) have `appearance-none` class but no visual indicator that they're dropdowns. The styling `w-full bg-zinc-950 border border-white/10 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-white text-xs font-medium focus-ring transition appearance-none` is identical to text inputs.
ideas.proposed_change:
Wrap each select in a relative div and add an absolute-positioned icon: `
expand_more
`. Add `pr-10` to select padding to avoid text overlap with icon.
ideas.user_benefit: Clear visual affordance that the element is a dropdown, consistent with UI conventions, reduced user confusion. Matches the pattern already used in GenerativeSidebar.

ideas.title: Toast Message Multi-line Support for Long Error Messages
ideas.description: Replace truncate class with line-clamp-2 for toast messages to prevent important error information from being cut off on smaller screens.
ideas.rationale: The Toast component uses `truncate` class (line 239) which cuts off longer messages with ellipsis. Combined with the `rounded-full` shape and uppercase tracking, important error messages or action confirmations may be illegible. Error messages especially need to be fully visible to help users understand what went wrong and take corrective action.
ideas.current_state: Toast.tsx line 239: message span has `text-[10px] sm:text-xs font-bold uppercase tracking-wider truncate flex-1` which truncates any text that doesn't fit in a single line. Messages like 'Voice: Failed to connect - check your API key in settings' would be cut off.
ideas.proposed_change: Replace `truncate` with `line-clamp-2` to allow 2 lines of text before truncating. Add `title={toast.message}` attribute for full text on hover. Consider changing container from `rounded-full` to `rounded-2xl` for messages exceeding 50 characters to better accommodate multi-line text.
ideas.user_benefit: Users can read complete error/success messages, especially important for error diagnostics and API key validation feedback. Reduces support requests from users who couldn't read the full error message.

ideas.title: Header Breadcrumb Context Display
ideas.description: Replace the empty center section in Header with contextual breadcrumbs or current location indicator when in Studio view.
ideas.rationale:
The Header component has an empty div (`
` at line 72-73) that takes up horizontal space but displays nothing. This creates visual imbalance and wastes valuable real estate that could help users understand their current location in the app, especially on larger screens.
ideas.current_state: Header.tsx line 72-73: Empty div between left (logo/back button/platform indicator) and right (refresh button) sections. The platformDisplay config exists and shows platform info, but no navigation context like current mode (Canvas, Templates, Media, LinkedIn).
ideas.proposed_change: Add a studioMode prop and display contextual breadcrumbs: `{onBackToDashboard && ({platformDisplay[activePlatform].name}/{studioMode})}`. Use subtle styling that doesn't compete with the platform indicator but provides additional context.
ideas.user_benefit: Users always know where they are in the app. Improved navigation understanding on larger screens. Better use of screen real estate. Reduces cognitive load when switching between modes.

ideas.title: Add Loading State Feedback to API Key Test Buttons
ideas.description: Enhance the API key test buttons in SettingsModal with proper loading spinners and disabled state handling during connection tests.
ideas.rationale: The SettingsModal has 'Test Connection' buttons for OpenRouter, OpenAI, and Replicate APIs (lines 349-355, 501-508, 546-555). While there's status tracking, the button text changes but lacks a visual spinner during the 'testing' state. Users may click multiple times thinking nothing is happening.
ideas.current_state: SettingsModal.tsx test buttons show 'Testing...' text when openRouterStatus === 'testing' (line 353) but use text-only feedback. The save button (lines 608-627) correctly shows a spinner (`sync`) during isSaving, but test buttons don't follow this pattern.
ideas.proposed_change: Update test buttons to match the save button pattern: `{openRouterStatus === 'testing' ? (<>syncTesting...) : 'Test Connection'}`. Also add `pointer-events-none` during testing to prevent double-clicks. The ConnectionStatus component shows status after, but inline feedback during is important.
ideas.user_benefit: Clear visual feedback that the connection test is in progress. Prevents accidental double-clicks that might trigger duplicate API calls. Consistent with save button behavior. Creates a more polished, responsive feel.
